title: Orders Border Security and Immigration Enforcement Changes
description_short: Orders Border Security and Immigration Enforcement Changes
description_medium: On January 25, 2017, Donald Trump signed Executive Order 13767, directing agencies to plan and build a physical wall on the southern border and expand immigration enforcement. The order called for detention while cases proceeded, expedited decisions on claims to remain, and prompt removal after claims were lawfully rejected. It also directed federal cooperation with state and local law enforcement. These were executive directives; the text alone does not show their implementation or outcomes.
description_long: Executive Order 13767, signed by Donald Trump on January 25, 2017, set out a broad agenda for border security and immigration enforcement. It directed agencies to begin planning and constructing a physical wall along the U.S.-Mexico border and called for additional personnel to support it. The order also instructed federal authorities to detain people apprehended on suspicion of violating federal or state law while their cases proceeded, expedite decisions on claims to remain in the country, and remove those whose claims were lawfully rejected after applicable proceedings. It encouraged cooperation with state and local law enforcement on federal immigration priorities. The order framed these measures as responses to border security and public-safety concerns. Its directions did not themselves establish how many people would be detained or removed, how much wall would be built, or how local agencies would participate. Those outcomes depended on later agency decisions, appropriations, and legal review. The supplied record documents the president’s directives and their stated enforcement aims; it does not provide implementation figures or the effects on particular migrants or border communities.
